sections.h2: Where is Roanoke, Virginia, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Roanoke is an independent city in Southwest Virginia, on the Roanoke River inside the Blue Ridge range, about 250 miles southwest of Washington, D.C. along Interstate 81 and roughly 50 miles north of the North Carolina line.

The Census Bureau estimates 99,111 residents for 2025, after a 2020 count of 100,011. That makes it the largest Virginia city west of Richmond and the center of a metro area of 315,251 people. The city covers 42.85 square miles, almost all of it land, and sits at an elevation of 974 feet.

Mill Mountain, a 1,700-foot peak with a 500-acre municipal park, stands inside the city limits and carries the Roanoke Star, an illuminated star 88.5 feet tall. The star gave Roanoke its nickname, the Star City of the South.

sections.h2: How did the railroad build Roanoke?
sections.html:
Roanoke began as the small town of Big Lick. In 1882 the Norfolk and Western Railway picked it for its headquarters and railroad shops, and within two years it was the City of Roanoke.

The population grew 22 times over in the 1880s, and the city later expanded through annexations from Roanoke County. Houses on the older blocks near downtown date from that boom, so age and deferred maintenance are common questions for sellers there.

The railroad era ended slowly. Norfolk and Western moved its headquarters out in 1982, and on May 18, 2020 Norfolk Southern closed its locomotive shops after 139 years of production. Parts of the former industrial land south of downtown have since been redeveloped.

Health care now leads the economy. Carilion Clinic is the city's top employer and the largest private employer west of Richmond, with more than 13,000 employees across nine hospitals in western Virginia.

Roanoke's 2024 annual financial report ranks its top employers as Carilion Roanoke Memorial Hospital, Roanoke City Public Schools, Carilion Services and the City of Roanoke, each with 1,000 or more employees. United Parcel Service follows with 500 to 999, and Walmart, the U.S. Postal Service, Virginia Transformer Corporation, the YMCA and Anthem each have 250 to 499.

  • Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine and Research Institute opened in 2007, and Radford University Carilion was established in 2019.
  • Regional manufacturers include Yokohama Tire, Volvo, Mack Trucks, Metalsa and Altec.
  • The city markets the area's outdoor recreation to recruit businesses and workers.

Hospital and university jobs bring in renters and buyers who often want to live close to the medical district. Sellers near that area should say so when describing their house.

sections.h2: Does Roanoke have a flooding problem?
sections.html:
Flooding is historically the main weather hazard in Roanoke. Heavy rain, often from the remnants of a hurricane, drains from the surrounding hills into the narrow Roanoke Valley.

The worst flood in city history came on November 4, 1985, when Hurricane Juan stalled over the area and ten people drowned in the valley. That led to a major flood reduction project by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, finished in 2012, which has limited damage from later storms. The most recent significant flood, in fall 2018, came when the remnants of Hurricane Michael dropped more than five inches of rain in a few hours.

  • Ask whether your parcel sits near the river or one of its creeks.
  • Look for water lines in crawl spaces and basements.
  • Keep records of any flood claims or drainage work.

We did not open a Roanoke city page on floodplain rules, so check with the city for requirements that apply to your lot.

sections.h2: What is Roanoke's weather like through the year?
sections.html:
Roanoke has a humid subtropical climate with four mild seasons, in USDA hardiness zone 7b. Monthly mean temperatures run from 37.9 degrees in January to 77.8 degrees in July.

The area averages 14.8 inches of snow per winter and about 6.1 days a year when the temperature stays at or below freezing. A December 2009 storm dropped 17 inches in a single event. Extremes range from 105 degrees in August 1983 to minus 12 degrees in December 1917.

Mountain-valley winters and humid summers tend to be hard on roofs, gutters and wood decks, and freezing can burst pipes in vacant houses. If yours has been empty, a quick walk-through will tell you what you are dealing with.

The city is divided into 49 neighborhoods, and its comprehensive plan sets a goal of developing them as villages, each with its own center and downtown acting as the center for the whole city.

Raleigh Court, near Grandin Village, is cited as a model, with a mix of housing around a commercial district anchored by the Grandin Theatre, the city's only surviving historic theater. Nine Roanoke neighborhoods, or portions of them, are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Ask the city whether your address falls in one before you plan exterior changes.

sections.h2: Does the outdoor setting matter for Roanoke home sellers?
sections.html:
It does, because the city markets itself on it. The Roanoke Valley has 26 miles of greenways, and the Blue Ridge Parkway runs just south of the city while the Appalachian Trail passes just north of it in Roanoke County.

Carvins Cove, at 12,700 acres, is the third-largest municipal park in America and lies in northeast Roanoke County and southwest Botetourt County. Smith Mountain Lake is several miles to the southeast. If your house is close to a trailhead, greenway or park, say so when you describe it.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Roanoke?
sections.html:
Roanoke City Public Schools runs the city's public schools. The two general enrollment public high schools are Patrick Henry, in the Raleigh Court area, and William Fleming, in Northwest Roanoke.

Virginia Western Community College is in the city, and the Roanoke Higher Education Center, opened in 2000, offers more than 150 programs. Roanoke College is in nearby Salem and Hollins University is in Roanoke County.

sections.h2: What does a Roanoke seller pay at closing, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of the sale price. The seller pays unless the buyer agrees to take on some or all of it, and the clerk must certify payment before the deed is recorded. See Virginia Code 58.1-802 for the text.

We did not open a Roanoke city page for tax rates, due dates or assessment appeals, so ask the city's real estate valuation and treasurer offices for current figures.

A cash sale here follows the same contract, title and deed steps without a lender. Tell us about the house, we review it, and any offer is based on the property as it stands. You do not repair or clean out first, and you can say no without owing anything.

faqs.q: What is the population of Roanoke, VA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 99,111 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 100,011.
Flooding is the city's main historical weather hazard, and the worst flood was on November 4, 1985. A flood reduction project was finished in 2012.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Roanoke?
faqs.a: Carilion Clinic is the top employer and the largest private employer west of Richmond, with over 13,000 employees.

faqs.q: How many neighborhoods does Roanoke have?
faqs.a: The city is divided into 49 neighborhoods, and nine of them, or parts of them, are on the National Register of Historic Places.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax in a Roanoke sale?
faqs.a: The seller, at 50 cents per $500 of the price, unless the buyer agrees to cover it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Roanoke house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy the house as is, and you do not need to fix anything first.
